text:
The de-identify step is wired in and the full suite passes (654 tests). I haven't run it against a live heimdall bridge or a real remote model. The benchmark agent hasn't replied yet.

**How it works now**
- The escalation request goes out with names, folder paths, filenames, emails, phone numbers, SSN-shaped ids and keys swapped for placeholders like `TERM_1`, `PATH_2` or `EMAIL_1`.
- Anything the Fold has read locally is masked too, because the existing registry of private terms feeds the masker.
- The username inside a home path (`/Users/<name>/…`) is masked, along with that username elsewhere in the text.
- Private IPs and `.local` / `.internal` / `.corp` / `.lan` hostnames are masked too.
- The real values stay on your machine, and the reply is mapped back before the agent sees it.
- If a scan of the masked text still finds a private detail, nothing is sent and the escalation errors out.
- The audit ledger records the masked bytes as a new grade, **masked**. It is not raw and not "sealed", because the code's logic is still readable.
- I rewrote the escalation line to say so: "Only your request and the code so far are sent, with names, folder paths, emails and keys swapped for placeholders. The code itself can still be read. Nothing else from your computer leaves it."
- A caller can pass `mask: false` to send as written; that is graded raw as before.

**What it doesn't catch**
- A stranger's name you typed into the request that the Fold never read.
- A public URL that is itself identifying.
- Whether a free model will copy `TERM_1` back intact. The tests prove my round-trip, not the model's behaviour.

**Heimdall free AI benchmark agent**
I asked it three things: which free models should lead the escalation order, whether any mangle opaque identifiers like `TERM_1`, and whether any free provider logs or trains on prompts. Its answer arrives automatically. I told it not to edit `fold-chat-client.js` or `fold-chat-deid.js`.

**Files**
- The new module is [fold-chat-deid.js](fold-chat-deid.js), with tests in [fold-chat-deid.test.mjs](fold-chat-deid.test.mjs).
- The wiring is in [fold-chat-client.js](fold-chat-client.js), [fold-chat-seal.js](fold-chat-seal.js) and [fold-chat.js](fold-chat.js), with small edits to the outbound summary, the feed wording and a CSS colour for the new grade in [index.html](index.html).
- `fold-chat.js` and `index.html` already had uncommitted changes from another session, so I kept my edits to a single line each.

Nothing is committed. Want me to wait for the benchmark reply and adjust the model order and placeholder format, or commit as is?

Lowercase names are now mostly caught, but not reliably. On a first untuned run of 28 names the de-identifier caught 4% before this change and 36% after. After fixes I made from that run's misses, the same set reads 68%, so that figure is no longer a clean test. The full suite passes (729 tests).

I wrote 42 informal asks and a second set of 28 after the detector's rules were fixed. They cover lowercase, SMS, Singlish, IRC handles, dialect, nicknames, Spanish and Turkish names, and names inside code, plus asks with no names. Nothing is committed. I tuned the cue rules on the first set, so its recall is optimistic.

| | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| First set (tuned) | 2% of 42 names | 74% |
| Second set, first untuned run | 4% of 28 | 36% |
| Second set after fixing its misses | | 68% (no longer held out) |

- **Over-masking:** none of the 10 asks with no names were touched. Plain words like timer, calculator, weather, tokyo and "miss you" were left alone.
- **Earlier count was wrong:** my earlier count of 3 of 37 for the first baseline was inflated by a bug in my check.

**The holograph can't do it for lowercase.** I ran the khora read on a four-sentence lowercase message full of names and it returned no referents. Its own doc says lowercase referents are not beings, and the English reader decides names by capital. Capitalised text works, and lowercase doesn't. That gap sits in the khora, not the-fold, so I haven't touched it.

**What the priors gave me:**
- The ethos organic-community corpus (Singapore, Indian and Sri Lankan SMS, IRC, Enron mail) supplied the informal spellings (gud, abt, lah). I kept a word as ordinary if it appears across several registers or in five or more different people's SMS. That separates shared informal spelling from someone's name.
- The corpus has no list of modern given names. A word is only marked as a name if it carries a capital mid-sentence in cased text. That gives 2,239 words, and it misses mike, kim, priya and tyrone.
- The finder, [fold-chat-informal.js](fold-chat-informal.js), flags a word as a name when it is not an ordinary word and sits in a name slot:
  - after a title or kin/role word (dr, auntie, treasurer, abuela)
  - after "for", "with", "call", "tell", "by" or "4"
  - after "name is", or before a possessive
  - in a list of names
  - in handle, identifier or street-address shapes
- It now always runs next to the khora read.

**On real SMS, IRC and mail text** (lowercased, no gold labels):
- **SMS:** about 5% of lines get flagged. The flagged words are mostly real names (vignesh, sarath, perera) plus SMS spellings and a few tech words (fone, xerox, dongle).
- **IRC:** flags are mostly nicks, which are correct, with tech words mixed in (ubuntu, compiz). It leans toward over-masking, which costs answer quality rather than privacy.

**Still missed:**
- A first name that is also an ordinary word, with no title or kin word before it ("ping mike", "my sponsor greg").
- Plural family names ("the wongs").
- Bare nicknames in a list with no cue.
- Names in languages with no cue words in the priors.

Those are pinned in tests so no one overclaims.

The finder reads from [fold-chat-priors-en.js](fold-chat-priors-en.js) (about 100 KB), which is generated by [eval/deid/build-vocab.mjs](eval/deid/build-vocab.mjs). That script also holds the cases and the runner, and reads ethos without changing it.

**Decisions for you:**
- **Khora gap:** want me to write it up for the khora repo? It would say the read returns nothing for lowercase text and the language face should treat register as informative.
- **Specimen-assembly guard:** the program-construction session has a stubbed `guard(request)` in `fillWithModel()` (`experiments/specimen-assembly/lib/solver.mjs`). It could be wired to `createDeid().maskAll` plus the fail-closed residual check. I left it alone because it isn't part of what you asked.
- **Benchmark agent:** still no reply, so the model-order and placeholder-format question is ope… [2 more chars at the transcript address]

text:
Yes, we can, and it's the strongest tier the seal already defines (`abstract`, then `worlds`). It works for some tasks, but not for the escalation path we've been building. I measured one version of it today.

**Where it fits**
- **Reasoning tasks:** if the job is "given these relations, what follows", the model needs only the structure. Hash every entity, send relations only, keep the key local. The reasoning engine (janus) already works that way, and I'd use it there.
- **Code and page writing:** the names and copy are the output. A page for "eleanor voss" has to say her name, and the model can't write her booking form from `H7f3…`. It could write the page with opaque slots and we fill them in locally, but that's the placeholder approach we have now.

**Why not a literal hash**
- **Hashes can be guessed:** a plain hash of a name can be recomputed from a list of names. It would need a secret key, or a random id issued per request, and the local map makes decryption unnecessary.
- **Stable ids link requests:** the same id across requests lets an observer build a profile over time. Per-request ids avoid that but lose continuity.
- **Structure still identifies:** a distinctive relationship graph can point to one person even with every name replaced. That's why the seal has the "possible worlds" decoys, which we haven't built.

**The real problem is recall.** "Convert all entities" only works if every entity is recognised, and that's the 68–74% we measured. Whatever the finder misses goes out in the clear, however it's hashed.

The inverse approach fixes that. Instead of blocking names we find, send only words we know are ordinary and make everything else opaque, using the same ordinary-word list from the ethos corpus. I measured it:

| | Names caught (first set / second set) | Words made opaque |
|---|---|---|
| Slot finder (current) | 74% / 68% | about 0 on asks with no names |
| Allowlist only | 79% / 75% | 17–19% of words |
| Both together | 90% / 75% | 17–19% of words |

On asks with no names, the allowlist turns "widget", "quiz" and "tracker" into opaque tokens too, which would hurt what the model writes. It also still misses names that are ordinary words ("kim", "mike", "mark").

**What I'd do:** keep the slot finder as the default, since it costs almost nothing in quality. Add the allowlist as an opt-in strict mode for a sensitive project, and use hashed relations only for reasoning tasks. Want me to build the strict mode?

The scripts are in `eval/deid/` (`allowlist.mjs`). Nothing is committed.

input: {"command":"cd /Users/mlacy/Documents/3.0/the-fold && cat > scripts/pii/measure.py <<'EOF'
"""Measure Presidio + spaCy on the informal, caseless cases (eval/deid/cases*.json).
A private name counts as caught when none of its distinctive words survives after every detected span is blanked.
Usage: scripts/pii/.venv/bin/python scripts/pii/measure.py [--model en_core_web_lg] [--threshold 0.35] [--lower]
  --lower   lowercase each ask first (the cases are already lowercase mostly; this makes it exact)
"""
import json, sys, argparse, pathlib
from presidio_analyzer import AnalyzerEngine
from presidio_analyzer.nlp_engine import NlpEngineProvider

ap = argparse.ArgumentParser()
ap.add_argument("--model", default="en_core_web_lg")
ap.add_argument("--threshold", type=float, default=0.35)
ap.add_argument("--lower", action="store_true")
ap.add_argument("--show", action="store_true")
a = ap.parse_args()

nlp = NlpEngineProvider(nlp_configuration={"nlp_engine_name": "spacy", "models": [{"lang_code": "en", "model_name": a.model}]}).create_engine()
eng = AnalyzerEngine(nlp_engine=nlp, supported_languages=["en"])
root = pathlib.Path(__file__).resolve().parents[2] / "eval" / "deid"

def blank(text, results):
    out = list(text)
    for r in results:
        for i in range(r.start, r.end):
            out[i] = "▮" if out[i] != " " else " "
    return "".join(out)

for fname in ["cases.json", "cases-heldout.json"]:
    cases = json.load(open(root / fname))["cases"]
    gold = caught = 0; over = 0; by = {}
    for c in cases:
        text = c["text"].lower() if a.lower else c["text"]
        res = [r for r in eng.analyze(text=text, language="en", score_threshold=a.threshold)]
        m = blank(text, res)
        for g in c["gold"]:
            gold += 1
            ok = g.lower().lstrip("@") not in m.lower()
            caught += ok
            b = by.setdefault(c["reg"], [0, 0]); b[1] += 1; b[0] += ok
        if not c["gold"]: over += len(res)
        if a.show: print(c["id"], [(text[r.start:r.end], r.entity_type, round(r.score, 2)) for r in res])
    print(f"{fname}: presidio+{a.model} recall {caught}/{gold} = {100*caught/gold:.0f}%   entities flagged in no-name asks: {over}")
    print("   " + " · ".join(f"{k} {v[0]}/{v[1]}" for k, v in by.items()))
EOF

- **Honest grading:** a request is graded "masked" only when the redactor judged it.

| Second set | 89% |

text:
We don't need to send normal words in every case, and the right design for a few of the cases below sends none.

**Where words aren't needed**
- **Reasoning over relations:** "who is related to whom, what follows". The Fold can read the ask locally, turn it into entities and relations, and send those with opaque ids. The reasoning engine already works this way.
- **Code assembled from specimens:** the program-construction session's experiment (`experiments/specimen-assembly`) says the model is called only for a gap the machinery has already named. Its request objects are plain JSON: the slot interface, the obligation ids and the failing operation sequences. There's no English in them, so there's nothing to de-identify. If hunt/swarm and holonic assembly work as you want, most requests would look like that. Provenance would then travel as the specimens' own ids, not as names.

**Where words are still needed**
- **Interpreting the ask:** if the Fold can't turn "make me a page for my cousin's hair shop" into a formal spec locally, the model has to read the sentence. The more the local reading can do, the fewer words leave.
- **Writing words:** a poem, copy or page text is the output, so the model needs enough language to write it. Even then the person's own details can be filled in locally afterwards, which is what the ids do now.
- **Meaningful names:** models lean on what identifiers and surrounding words mean. A function called `retry` tells it what to write, and `f7` doesn't. I haven't measured how much quality drops when everything is opaque. I can measure it cheaply on your local models: the same coding tasks with meaningful names versus fully opaque ones. If the drop is small, there's little reason to send readable words at all.

**What this suggests**
1. **Default for anything that can be formalised:** send only the formal gap or relations, with no natural-language words.
2. **Everything else:** keep the redactor and per-turn ids as built.
3. **`open` mode:** it would only cover the cases where words are unavoidable.

The opaque-versus-meaningful measurement is the one to run first, because it tells us how far tier 1 can go. Want me to run it on the local models?

A small, reproducible harness that drives the REAL chat page headlessly (Playwright), records every turn from the
persisted session JSON, and scores it against gold facts that were checked against Wikipedia.

## Files

| file | what |
|---|---|
| `cases.json` | 73 cases / 83 turns in 9 strata, each with a one-line rationale, gold answer, gold check(s), gold URL(s). Built by `build-cases.mjs` (the multilingual block is generated from one table). |
| `run.mjs` | the driver. One fresh browser context per case, model chosen through Settings -> Models (the app's own drawer), composer polled until enabled, session read from `localStorage["fold-chat:sessions"]`. Writes `raw/<label>__<case>__r<k>.json` (resuma
| `lib/snapshot.mjs` | freezes the working tree into `eval/.app/` (sha256 of every file in `.app/_meta.json`) and serves it on a private port, so concurrent edits by other people cannot change a run mid-way. |
| `score.mjs` | deterministic metrics + merges `judgments.json` (my per-case reading, with a reason) -> `results.json`. |
| `controls.mjs` | offline gate tests (no browser, no model): feeds hand-written true/false sentences to the app's own `fold-chat-ground.js` against real Wikipedia text -> `controls-results.json`. |
| `worksheet.mjs` | lays out answer sentences beside the evidence for hand-labelling -> `labels.json`. |
| `judgments.json`, `labels.json` | the human (reading) part of the scoring, kept auditable. |
| `run-all.sh` | the full sequence: default model (all cases) -> sealed frontier model (subset) -> 3x repeats of the flakiness subset. |

## Rerun

```
node eval/build-cases.mjs                         # (re)generate cases.json
node eval/run.mjs --resnap                        # default model (autoPick = gemma2:2b), all cases, snapshot the CURRENT tree first
```

text:
I looked for one in the repo's own evidence and didn't find a case where a large model is needed to answer. The cases I did find where a model earns its place are about proposing, not answering.

**What the data says (the Fold's own studies)**

| Evidence | Result |
|---|---|
| 221-ask study of snip-with-provenance answers, no model | 148 of 199 answerable asks (74%) satisfied with no model |
| Asks my reading flagged as "needs-model" | 5 of 199 |
| Failures | 46 |
| Frontier model (claude-sonnet-4-6) in the full app, 33 turns | 73%, versus 78% for the small local model (83 turns, not the same asks) |

- **The 5 "needs-model" asks don't hold up as large-model cases.**
  - "100°F in Celsius" is arithmetic, and the Fold already computes that without a model.
  - "How do I renew my driver's license" needs a clarifying question, because the ask names no state.
  - "When is the next Coachella" needs date logic (2026 is past) plus the date.
  - That leaves two: "best time to visit Japan" and "best laptop for programming", which are cross-source recommendations. A set of attributed snips showing where sources agree and differ is arguably the right answer there.
- **The 46 failures are mostly reader and retrieval bugs, not missing intelligence.**
  - Code blocks dropped by the page reader.
  - JS-challenge pages read as text.
  - Wrong-sense pages.
  - The coverage gate over-refusing when the answer was already held.
  - The frontier model didn't beat the small one because retrieval was the bottleneck.
- I also looked at 22 of your real first prompts in this project. Most were things snipping or tools can do: "what's the latest on the Lincoln VP glitch", git-ignore the downloaded sites, test the app in the browser, a cost lookup for a VM.

**The narrow case where a model seems irreducible**

Your prompt about defining the VOIDs of every query precisely, "using all the operators and perhaps the other faces", is the clearest one I found. It asks for new structure with no source to cite. The same goes for novel code that fills a gap no stored example covers. Both need a proposer. Their results can then be checked mechanically, with provenance marked "generated, verified by X". That matches your specimen-assembly design: the model enters only at a named gap.

**What this doesn't prove**
- The 22 prompts are a small sample, and my classification of them is my own reading, not a measurement.
- Nothing here tests whether a large model proposes better than your engine does, which is the reasoning question from earlier.

**To make it solid:** pre-register about 40 real asks from your transcripts. Label each as snip-only, deterministic tool, or needs a proposer, ideally by two readers blind to each other, then check the ones labelled "needs a proposer" against the engine. Want me to set that up?

**Your Pyodide question**
- I tested it directly in Pyodide 0.28 under Node. spaCy, thinc and presidio-analyzer all failed to install. spaCy and its dependencies have no WebAssembly build there.
- The spaCy part is what gave the recall on lowercase names, so as it stands Pyodide can't replace the Python server.
- **Untested:** I haven't tried Presidio's pattern recognizers alone without spaCy. They mostly duplicate the shape rules we already have in JavaScript.
- **Alternative:** run a small NER model directly in the page, via transformers.js or ONNX. It needs model downloads from Hugging Face, and I'd measure it on the lowercase cases first. Do you approve those downloads?
- Until then the local server stays the standard.
